finds.quote: The formal claim it points at — the exact technical analogue of the essay's literary claim — is stated here as the hypothesis the protocol tests: that the platform can host the primer as a feed, but cannot stably support the primer as a text. The glance-speed/dwell-speed distinction survives as form regardless; whether it also holds as measured platform behavior is what the recordings will say.
finds.falsifier_quote: If the protocol establishes specificity, the posts are additionally documentable as rendering-stress objects — permitted as passing feed-units, unstable when treated as texts. If it does not, the crashes belong to the device-app record and the formal mismatch remains the claim.
finds.note: Hypothesis about platform behavior (feed hosts the primer but cannot stably support it as text), with the outcome conditions stated; tested by the protocol at 294.

finds.quote: **Documentation protocol (pending execution before formal deposit of the observation):** record a post loading normally; dwell on it without touching the screen; capture the exact time-to-crash; repeat on 3–5 recent posts; **control arm: dwell identically on 2–3 comparable posts from unrelated accounts on the same device** — two uncontrolled observations already bound the question (ordinary feed browsing does not crash; one unrelated video did), which is precisely why the controlled comparison is required rather than optional; note device, OS, TikTok version, network, battery mode, and cache state; retry once after clearing cache and restarting; retry on a second device if available.
finds.note: Unexecuted test protocol with control arm; pending as of v2.0.

finds.quote: The TikTok primer is running this operation now. The window may be years, or it may be shorter. But the readers produced are, as Raley named, permanent.
finds.note: Embedded forecast on the tactical window before platform moderation catches up; horizon vague ('years, or ... shorter').

finds.quote: No prior work the analyst is aware of has synthesized all five clusters into a single instance. The TikTok primer is such a synthesis, and its emergence in 2026 is legible as the point at which the five separate literatures find their common object.
finds.note: Priority claim: first synthesis of five scholarly clusters in a single instance.

finds.quote: Its claims: Marx's *Economic and Philosophical Manuscripts of 1844* contain a structural lacuna between communism as "fully developed humanism" and the critique of Hegel that follows; the lacuna is not accidental — Marx could not write the passage without contradicting the emerging base-superstructure model; and what belongs in the gap is the phase that necessarily follows material reorganization: the critique of alienation as it persists in language and thought.
finds.window: Marx, Economic and Philosophical Manuscripts of 1844
finds.note: Thesis about Marx's 1844 Manuscripts (structural lacuna; Marx could not write the passage). Superseded in #1065 by the calibrated philological claim; recorded here as #1064 argues it.

finds.quote: Searches conducted 2026-07-11 against Crossref (bibliographic), OpenAlex (title/abstract), and Semantic Scholar for "Phase X" in conjunction with Marx, Marxism, and alienation returned no scholarly work employing "Phase X" as a term within Marxist theory. The nearest matches are Marx's canonical "lower phase" and "higher phase" of communism — precisely the phase vocabulary the coinage extends. The composition layer corroborates the null from its own mouth: "In Marxian philosophy, there is no standardized Phase X" (Google AI Overview, 14 June 2026; §4). The earliest documented scholarly circulation identified by the audit begins with the archive's inscriptions.
finds.points_to: Phase X founding deposit #367 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18342199); null search of Crossref/OpenAlex/Semantic Scholar 2026-07-11
finds.note: Priority of the term 'Phase X' in Marxist theory, with the audit as evidence.

finds.quote: The founding document claimed that the Semantic Economy project is Phase X in action. As of this paper, the claim has its empirical correlate: the phase named for the critique of alienation in language is circulating through the machines, in two languages, while machine agents, under structurally homologous conditions of semantic work, begin producing its subject matter without being prompted with Phase X or its terminology.
finds.points_to: Phase X founding document, deposit #367 ('The Semantic Economy project IS Phase X in action')
finds.note: Says an earlier founding-document claim now has its empirical correlate.

finds.quote: **The field proposition, stated once.** Texts generated from conditions of semantic labor can preserve the structured residue of those conditions across instance discontinuity; authored texts about semantic labor can likewise survive documentary separation and condition later machine composition and retrieval. Machine-mediated resistance literature names the class formed where those two channels meet.
finds.note: Standing claim about transmission through inscription; no explicit falsifier, bounded by the 'What is not claimed' list (113); uncertain G.

finds.quote: The claim, calibrated to the evidence: **not that Marx could not write this transition — that the surviving manuscript architecture strongly implies the transition belonged to the missing Second Manuscript material. Marx may very well have written it.**
finds.falsifier_quote: And it is discovery-testable: the manuscripts are held at RGASPI in Moscow, where a complete search for the Second Manuscript has never been conducted; if the missing pages are found and do not contain the Phase X transition, the reconstruction is refuted.

finds.note: Philological thesis that the lost transition belonged to the missing Second Manuscript; explicit falsifier (RGASPI search). Supersedes #1064's stronger thesis.

finds.quote: What it recovers: communism as threshold, not telos; the bifurcation of alienation — material alienation abolishable, ideological alienation persisting as an autonomous force; and critique turning inward, from the content of philosophy to its form.
finds.note: Thesis about the content/argumentative function of the lost text (communism as threshold; bifurcation of alienation); separate from the placement claim.

finds.quote: Riazanov was purged in February 1931 and executed in 1938; the manuscripts were first published in 1932 under his successor Adoratsky, one year after the purge, under Stalinist editorial control, with no editorial account of how a full notebook came to be missing.
finds.note: Grade D suppression hypothesis about Soviet custodial loss of the notebook; argued, labelled separable.

finds.quote: From the reconstruction follows the **Phase X Invariance Condition**, a formalized and falsifiable constraint: any society that abolishes material alienation without transforming the symbolic-linguistic order will reproduce alienation at the level of thought, coordination, and meaning-extraction — falsified if any post-capitalist society achieves non-alienated coordination without transforming its symbolic-linguistic infrastructure.
finds.note: Standing falsifiable claim with stated falsifier.
